requirement_text.REQ-149: Design requirement settling OQ-1: how a Lua script execution gets a configurable memory limit. Deliverable: lib/letflow/design/req149-lua-memory-limit.md naming one RECOMMENDED MECHANISM, stating which of LUA-09's two clauses it satisfies, rejecting :max_instructions, and disposing of the decision 0014 addendum question.

task.description:
Validate CODE-DESIGNER's artefact at lib/letflow/design/req149-lua-memory-limit.md on branch feature/WF02-REQ149-20260826. Check out the feature branch before reading.

Gate criteria:
1. Every acceptance criterion from REQ-149 is covered by the artefact:
   - Names exactly one RECOMMENDED MECHANISM (not a pros/cons list)
   - Quotes a real search of deps/lua/ source (not just docs) for memory-limit options
   - For :max_heap_size candidate, quotes a real run showing what happens when exceeded
   - States explicitly which of LUA-09's two clauses are satisfied and which are not
   - Explicitly rejects :max_instructions as a memory proxy with decision 0014 OQ-1 citation
   - States whether a decision 0014 addendum is needed (and if so, writes it)
   - No lib/letflow/engine/ file and no mix.exs change made
2. No implementation code present (this is a design-only requirement)
3. The design is unambiguous enough for REQ-156 to implement against
acceptance_criteria: All six REQ-149 acceptance criteria are verified against the actual artefact
PASS only if all six are met
FAIL with specific missing coverage if any criterion fails
